citation: Alanson Skinner, "The Mascoutens or Prairie Potawatomi Indians, Part III — Mythology and Folklore", Bulletin of the Public Museum of the City of Milwaukee, vol. 6, no. 3, pp. 327-411 (Milwaukee, 22 January 1927).
author: Alanson Skinner, from Prairie Potawatomi narrators, among them John Nuwi, who 'said that he was born near Fort Dearborn, Chicago' (p. 408)
describes_date: Stories and recollections told to Skinner in the 1910s-1920s; Nuwi's own life runs back to the 1830s
repository: Internet Archive, item mascoutensorprai0006skin (Trent University copy).
locator: p. 379 (in a story, two brothers 'prepared camps and arbors' for a feast); pp. 408-09 (John Nuwi's biographic note; 'they put me out under a bough arbor'). Read in the Internet Archive's OCR text, located by the printed page numbers.
access_notes: Fetched 2026-11-03 from archive.org as the djvu text (T-3342). Rights not checked; only short quotation is used, no asset is derived.
note: The Potawatomi's own word, through an ethnographer a century later, that a camp of theirs had its arbors of boughs beside its lodges. T-3342 reads it for that and nothing else; the story on p. 379 is a story, not a description of a camp at Chicago.
what_it_supplies: the bough arbor as part of a Potawatomi camp, in a Potawatomi narrator's words (pp. 379, 409)
what_it_does_not_supply: any description of the camp of August 1812, or of an arbor's size or making
anything the 1812 scene stages: the ceremonies the stories tell of are not drawn
